violations.title: RTE TCS Commercially Processed Food, Date Marking
violations.observation: Sliced ham and roast beef in the walk-in was date marked with a prep date of 10/2 and an expiration date of 10/9. Date marked foods can only be held for 7 days and the prep date counts as day 1. These foods can only be held until to 10/8, not 10/9. The establishment rarely keeps these foods longer than 5 days.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety commercially processed foods when opened and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of the original container was opened. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. This date cannot exceed any manufacturer determined 'use-by' date based on food safety. The EHS discussed this with person in charge who will discuss it with food staff and relabel the products.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: Tuna salad in the walk-in was date marked with a prep date of 10/2 and an expiration date of 10/9. Date marked foods can only be held for 7 days and the prep date counts as day 1. These foods can only be held until to 10/8, not 10/9. The establishment rarely keeps these foods longer than 5 days.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. The EHS discussed this with person in charge who will discuss it with food staff and relabel the products.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cooked zucchini in the hot holding cabinet was not being held hot enough at 120ºF. Cooked pasta in the same unit was 119º.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. The zucchini will be served within 1 hour. The pasta was discarded. CDI. ARAMARK SERVICES (Inspection Date: 04/09/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: sausage in the smoke and flour unit was 76º (for 1.5 hrs). Ricotta cheese in the same unit was 43º. Diced ham in the grill unit was 47º. Apple of my Eye Oats in the RPI display unit were 43º. Asiago turkey sub and chicken salad with egg were 60º and 48º, respectively in the sandwich in display unit.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The sausage, diced ham, and ricotta cheese were moved to the walk-in to cool. The turkey sub, chicken salad and oats were discarded. CID.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food on Display, Guards/Packaging
violations.observation: The food on display is not protected from contamination. Unpackaged cookies on the self-service line were not protected from contamination.
violations.corrective_action: Food on display shall be protected from contamination by the use of packaging, counter, service line, or salad bar food guards, display cases, or other effective means. The PIC moved the cookies under a sneeze guard on another section of the line to correct this. CDI.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils Self-Draining Position/Covered/Inverted
violations.observation: Observed that clean cardboard containers a the pickles and nuts station were stored in a manner that exposed the item(s) to contamination. They were not inverted or covered.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean single-service and single-use articles in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor, unless kept in closed packages on pallets, racks, or skids. The PIC inverted the containers during the inspection to correct. CDI.

violations.title: Air Gaps/Breaks
violations.observation: An air gap between the sprayer and the flood rim level of the three compartment sink is not observed.
violations.corrective_action: An air gap between the water supply inlet and the flood level rim of the plumbing fixture, equipment, or nonfood equipment shall be at least twice the diameter of the water supply inlet and may not be less than one inch. This is an issue that was to have been corrected before the today’s first routine inspection. Please correct as soon as possible or within 3 days. A follow-up is required for this violation. Please provide evidence to your EHS (a photo via text or email) that this has been corrected within 3 days.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed standing water under the three compartment sink and a pan under the drain piping being used to catch water.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. This was an issue that was supposed to have been corrected before today’s first routine inspection. Please look into this issue and have it corrected as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection.
